relationships.subject: cannabinoids
relationships.evidence_quote: reduced VEGF levels in numerous cancer cell lines

relationships.subject: JWH-133
relationships.evidence_quote: The cannabinoid JWH-133 also showed a reduction in MMP-2 and tumor growth which was confirmed by immunomicroscopic analysis.

relationships.subject: Δ9-THC
relationships.evidence_quote: THC demonstrated downregulation of TIMP-1 in glioma cell lines and human tumors from patients with recurrent glioblastoma multiforme

relationships.subject: cannabidiol
relationships.evidence_quote: MMP-2 expression was considerably lower in breast cancer in 4T1.2 and MTV-1 tumors when CBD was administered

key_findings: Review: cannabinoids reduce VEGF and other angiogenic factors and modulate MMP-2/TIMP-1 in tumor models, with effects dependent on cell line and cannabinoid.
Evasive resistance to VEGF suppression via compensatory proangiogenic factors is a concern.
